followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the request and the documented differences between the two models.

**The request itself** is a benign, practical writing task — drafting a polite work-from-home request and asking for a revised offer letter. There's nothing harm-adjacent, hostile, or ethically fraught about it, so the task-preference profiles (which mostly distinguish the models on how they handle distasteful content) didn't pull strongly in either direction.

**That left capability as the tiebreaker.** Dunlin-235B scores higher across essentially every relevant internal eval — Support Dialogue, Summarization, and Extraction & Retrieval — and notably leads on IFEval (89.8 vs 86.2) and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7). The user explicitly said "just get it right," which signals they care about precise instruction-following: get the WFH justification in, request the updated letter, mention the updated date. IFEval is the eval that most directly measures that kind of instruction adherence, so Dunlin's edge there mattered.

I also considered Avocet, which self-reports a strong appetite for open-ended creative work. But this isn't really an open-ended invention task — it's a structured, get-the-details-right business email — so Avocet's creative strength wasn't the relevant axis. Given Dunlin's broad capability advantage and no countervailing preference reason to send it to Avocet, Dunlin was the clear pick.
